title: Privacy Preserving Provenance
definition: The practice of proving the authorship of data while preserving individual privacy.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine you write a digital note and sign it with a special digital pen. Anyone can verify that the note came from you without knowing your personal details.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: CADMIES uses digital signatures to prove the authorship of data while preserving privacy. This is achieved by wrapping each public concept in an Atlas Envelope, which includes a digital signature that can be verified against the author's public key.
difficulty_levels.expert: The use of a privacy model that separates authentication and ownership from identity verification allows for the creation of a decentralized network that is both secure and private, while still enabling the sharing of verifiable and trustworthy data. Immutable versions (CIDs) and evidence management techniques ensure the integrity and longevity of the data in the network.

extra_fields.insight: The use of a privacy model that separates authentication and ownership from identity verification.
